config.monster-stories.f6b3925ffa: Deliver all three commissions, then choose a Firefly Laser Rifle or Hovercraft at the board. The gift is yours—take it out and see more of the forest.
config.monster-stories.165fe73a3f: Now I remember more than the monsters' names. I remember the lives they're waiting to get back to.
config.monster-stories.4983223c30: The flowerpots sold out! Something that caused trouble can turn out to be just what someone needs.
config.monster-stories.04c0394b16: I'll change the sign: exclusive breathable flowerpots. No battles today—just business!
config.monster-stories.feaaa7d1f2: Nightleaf needs pots for moonflowers. Why not set up your stalls together?
config.monster-stories.3a2c4ef93c: I kept breaking dishes while practicing washing up, so I made my own. But my claws are too big. Every bowl has a hole.
config.monster-stories.65425bd854: Let's ask the maker first: are these bowls, or flowerpots?
config.monster-stories.72411be946: The stalls are safe. The pottery label says, “May leak soup. Excellent for flowers.”
config.monster-stories.7f5714f71b: I'll pass both signposts. My handheld weapon and the vehicle's main gun can help while I drive.
config.monster-stories.eb45e5b6d4: The crates hold old equipment everyone repaired. Not loot—gifts the neighbors put together, piece by piece.
config.monster-stories.3943330ad1: The fiercest one is most afraid of bad reviews. Borrow a Hovercraft for the cargo. It handles land and water, and its main gun can protect the route.
config.monster-stories.a4141ca861: No patrols on weekends—we run a market! Nightleaf sells flower tags, the Owl Lord fixes lamps, and Iron-Tusk makes bowls.
config.monster-stories.15c9f4e8c4: Clear the market square and protect the stalls
config.monster-stories.9c53e79133: Drive the Hovercraft past the signposts to deliver the crates
config.monster-stories.0408002792: The market's slowest sellers aren't equipment, but Iron-Tusk's little clay bowls. He wants to hide his stall where nobody can see it.
config.monster-stories.ad71797f14: Here's your pay. When the flowers open, I'll save him a place too.
config.monster-stories.bf25882474: Tell him in person next time. Your wishes deserve to be heard, even by a boss.
config.monster-stories.b2386584b5: He really came to cover my shift—with two round leaves for glasses.
config.monster-stories.2bfbf5c4c3: The path is clear. A note on a branch says, “Write leave requests in large letters. Bosses get farsighted too.”
config.monster-stories.3fc8b892a7: I'll cover tonight. Please clear the shift-change path so he doesn't miss the flowers.
config.monster-stories.7cbfeea6f2: One of you was afraid to ask, the other couldn't read it, and somehow that made an extra shift.
config.monster-stories.20589fca24: “Time to rest”? From the treetop I read “Time for a test”! You should have said something. I lost my reading glasses.
config.monster-stories.f5df7d8e31: Visit both shift-change points first so nobody waits for you, then deliver the original note.
config.monster-stories.46bf0c63b5: He always reads letters from the highest branch. I'm afraid to fly that close.
config.monster-stories.2dc8a079d4: Maybe we should ask him face to face. I'll borrow a Patrol Car and deliver the shift-change notice for you.
config.monster-stories.1a94d927d1: I wrote “time to rest tonight,” and the Owl Lord approved a patrol assignment. Does he dislike me?
config.monster-stories.4cbe2bcbc0: Clear the shift-change path so Nightleaf can enjoy the flowers
config.monster-stories.119798c233: Hand the leave request to the Owl Lord
config.monster-stories.129d4fa4f1: Deliver notices at both shift-change points
config.monster-stories.48e1cd4fdc: Hear Nightleaf's story about the leave request
config.monster-stories.7de5c71994: Nightleaf wants one night off to see the moonflower, which blooms for just one night. The Owl Lord has approved the request as a patrol route instead.
config.monster-stories.7dd186c119: Your pay is here. Two more neighbors have commissions, and an equipment gift awaits at the market.
config.monster-stories.0820eb438f: So that roar might have been embarrassment after all.
config.monster-stories.24c1a70146: He offered to wash up? I'll use wooden bowls tomorrow.
config.monster-stories.b734e6d74b: Tell him this: I'll do the dishes tomorrow. Don't mention that I've already broken three.
config.monster-stories.8c3c7893d0: Sprig just doesn't want you going hungry. Soft food, less salt, plenty of care.
config.monster-stories.0c6d672ec9: Keep it down! I've practiced “thank you” all morning, but it still sounds like a declaration of war.
config.monster-stories.efcf36738b: So the chef isn't celebrating the boss today. The boss is secretly preparing a thank-you gift.
config.monster-stories.f96a501ea4: The basket is intact. There's a crooked heart on the note: Happy birthday, Chef!
config.monster-stories.41fdd097f5: The borrowed Firefly Laser can pierce a row of targets. I'll move to the side and clear the path.
config.monster-stories.c9a0b4d883: Tender leaves and soft acorns. Wild slimes stole the lunch basket on the way. Could you get it back?
config.monster-stories.0acff6f1da: Yes. His tusks can flip a car, but he can't bite through a hard rice ball. Come collect the ingredients on the path first.
config.monster-stories.7cee75ef42: Your commission is to deliver lunch, not fight him?
config.monster-stories.bcc2275957: Iron-Tusk said nobody should come near today. I bet he shouted “less company” when he meant “less salt” again!
config.monster-stories.2ceb159b32: Drive off the food thieves and recover the lunch basket
config.monster-stories.11c47aece5: Find Sprig and collect the low-salt ingredients
config.monster-stories.68e07c458f: Iron-Tusk roars every afternoon. The sprout-slime chef says it's not a battle cry—it's his stomach growling.
config.monster-stories.80adec47fa: Collect this story's first-clear rewards and return borrowed equipment. Complete the set to choose one permanent item at the commission board.
config.monster-stories.b2634a7d30: This time, we heard the monsters' stories
config.monster-stories.235d9eee51: Return to the commission board to hear the reply

config.monster-stories.c91ecb2b78: Who says monsters don't have lives of their own?

balance.dc9dee60bd: Try out resource rules and see when players upgrade or buy equipment. Editing a candidate does not change saves or publish changes to the game.
balance.1a4a04c047: Keep Recommended · 8–12 Hours, Mixed Combat · No Logging, and standard efficiency. Select Run 100 Simulations. The 900-minute limit represents 15 hours.
balance.2a8082f9a7: For the standard route, first check that P50 is 8–12 hours. Then inspect incomplete runs and the longest late-game gap. Aim for 0/100 late-game gaps over 12 minutes.
balance.f07fbe861e: Select Keep as Baseline at the bottom, change just one parameter category, and run again. Adjust prices, production, and stats separately to see causes clearly.
balance.d1a3c666fe: Switch balance charts between coins, wood, and other resources. Compare income, spending, and shortfalls. Expand Activity Returns to see which activities pay better.
balance.7e55fba4bd: Use the combat benchmark to compare milestones such as 4 → 5 and 9 → 10. Then retest at Low Efficiency ×0.65 and on forest-first or realm-first routes.
balance.7ed0a531d4: Export Configuration saves parameters. Report JSON keeps detailed results; CSV is useful for spreadsheet analysis. Deployment still requires updating project configuration and verifying it.
balance.d060cff6a5: Which Parameter Should I Change First?
balance.667f785579: Check base cost, cost exponent, and per-upgrade coin caps under Upgrade Costs. Lower costs, then inspect gaps and purchase times.
balance.72136c79a7: New Equipment Takes Too Long to Buy
balance.a7a8d671dd: Identify whether coins, materials, or eligibility are missing. Check recipes, production, or challenge thresholds accordingly. Saving coins cannot solve an eligibility requirement.
balance.2cbd06d938: Raise the Forest Monsters wood ratio, or lower the Upgrade Costs wood ratio. One increases production; the other reduces spending.
balance.f4b52c7f68: Check Growth Multipliers and compare time to kill and effective damage in the firing test. Cheaper costs do not mean larger stat gains.
balance.bcc0237fc6: Plenty of Money, but No Recent Upgrade
balance.56e5e9419e: Check spending strategy, visit interval, and expedition budget. Long challenges prevent permanent upgrades mid-run, and bulk spending can exhaust available upgrades early.
balance.af9e98d32b: Defaults assume workshop visits about every 5 minutes and short, 6-minute realm expeditions. These model player behavior, not cooldowns or forced waits. Revalidate after changing them. Do not raise assumed kill efficiency just to meet targets.
balance.9daad2e7de: Edits affect only the candidate. The game reads the repository's production configuration.
balance.27202871b8: Defaults use workshop visits every 5 minutes, more often early on, and 6-minute realm expeditions. Decide whether to return before each stage; failures and return trips consume time. Leaving restarts at stage 1. Permanent upgrades happen only in the forest. Visits model route choices, not game cooldowns. Increase the expedition budget to examine the cost of longer climbs.
balance.0e8803e0af: Purchases follow the list from top to bottom. Choose a category, then an equipment name. Use Move Up and Move Down to reorder. Later items wait until earlier purchases are made; owned items are skipped.
balance.d606582002: Starting Progress JSON (empty for a fresh save)
balance.fb7d0d1eb7: Expand a category to edit. Parameter descriptions explain their purpose; select Effect of Changes for direction and limits. A ratio of 0.3 means 30%; a growth multiplier of 1.08 means an 8% increase.
balance.992dfdabb2: After editing, select Apply JSON to validate and update the candidate, then rerun the simulation. Exports use version 2. Importing version 1 retains old costs without automatically applying recommended caps.

balance.5e5eb7cd08: About 10%, 50%, or 90% of samples finish the main goal within these times. P50 is the median, not the mean.
balance.1509cba3e2: Runs that remain incomplete at the simulation limit. They still count toward percentiles. Not Completed Within Limit does not mean zero hours.

balance.89a021644d: Compare two levels in the same scenario, including reloads, charging, and summons. The boss durability target does not simulate boss skills.
balance.4cbdb8f67a: Effective DPS is damage actually dealt per second, excluding overkill. Lower first-kill time and more kills are usually better. Higher damage per shot does not always mean better sustained damage; account for reloads, pellets, and summons.
balance.bbb0de393c: Keep one result, change parameters, and rerun. Use the same player route when comparing prices or production; changing efficiency compares player types. The comparison stays only in this page's memory. Export before refreshing.
balance.0e26d8b637: Configuration JSON lets you resume tuning. Report JSON contains this run's parameters, route, and detailed results; CSV supports spreadsheet analysis. arrival.title: Day One · A Forest Handover
arrival.ride: The little electric scooter rolls slowly along the forest path. It is your first day on the job.
arrival.dialogue.welcome: Hold on, the ranger’s cottage is just ahead. I’m Old Pine. I’ve patrolled these woods most of my life, and today I finally retire.
arrival.dialogue.reason: You must be the new ranger taking my place! The forest station accepted your application and sent you here to look after these woods. This little cottage will be your home.
arrival.dialogue.duty: Patrol the paths, gather timber, and keep the facilities in good repair. When our forest neighbors need help, they leave requests on the notice boards.
arrival.dialogue.waves: Monsters come out of the deep woods in waves. Get a weapon ready, then protect the camp. After a few waves, you’ll face a lord. Take your time—the first watch begins after you make your first pistol.
arrival.dialogue.realms: Those glowing entrances lead to realms. The Tower tests how far you can climb, Guardian asks you to protect the altar, and Expedition lets you discover more equipment. Go when you’re ready.
arrival.dialogue.workshop: The Weapons Workshop beside the cottage needs repairs. Use the chainsaw to gather timber: {p0} wood to repair it, then {p1} to make an Acorn Pistol. Walk up to a tree and the saw works automatically. The separate Vehicle Workshop to the west handles vehicles.
arrival.dialogue.gifts: This chainsaw, these cottage and workshop keys, and the scooter are yours now. You can use your handheld weapon while riding; the scooter has no turret. I’ll walk back to the village. Take good care of our forest!
arrival.dismount: Home at last · Time to get off
arrival.leave: Old Pine waves goodbye and walks back to the village. It is your turn to look after the forest.
